feed.title: Peabody Complaints Archive
feed.subtitle: Service charges, disclosure and accountability in social housing.
feed.rights: This site is independent of Peabody Trust and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or operated by Peabody Trust.

entry.title: What does Peabody have to hide?
entry.summary: Nearly two years of correspondence about one question: what are residents being charged for? Lost requests, contradictory complaint responses, an internal review, missed deadlines and a conviction.

entry.title: Who is the worst housing association?
entry.summary: We counted Housing Ombudsman reports, adjusted for landlord size and checked the regulator's lowest grade. Three tests, three different answers, and one name that appeared every time.

entry.title: How Shared Ownership Is Being Sold in a Difficult Leasehold Market
entry.summary: Housing associations are offering deposit contributions, cashback and temporary service-charge subsidies on shared-ownership homes. What those incentives offset, and what expires.

entry.title: The Staircase That Goes Nowhere: You Own 30%. You Pay 100%.
entry.summary: Shared owners hold a fraction of the equity but the whole service-charge liability. What the data does and does not show about staircasing, cost and control.

entry.title: Who Signed the Letter Calling for Housing Association Reform?
entry.summary: Twenty-nine MPs and peers signed a July 2026 letter to the Housing Minister on housing association accountability. A factual guide to who they are and what experience they bring.

entry.title: Peabody Broke the Law. A Resident Had to Prosecute It.
entry.summary: After nearly two years of unanswered requests, failed complaints and inaccurate assurances to an MP, a leaseholder privately prosecuted one of England's largest housing associations. Peabody pleaded guilty.

entry.title: Leasehold: The Market Is Finally Pricing In The Risk
entry.summary: Government, the courts and the market are converging on the same diagnosis of leasehold. The question is who pays for the slow transition.

entry.title: An Open Letter to the King on the 2026 Honours
entry.summary: An open letter objecting to a CBE awarded to Peabody Trust's CEO for services to social housing, written by a Peabody leaseholder.

entry.title: The Three Closed Doors: A Stress Test of Leasehold Accountability
entry.summary: Parliament built three safeguards for leaseholders. A former banker asks whether any of them actually function under stress.

entry.title: Missing Information and the Service Charge Maze
entry.summary: How one accidental email built a residents' association, and what two and a half years of asking Peabody for the accounts revealed.

entry.title: Written Evidence to Parliament on the Leasehold Reform Bill
entry.summary: Written evidence to the HCLG Committee on the draft Commonhold and Leasehold Reform Bill, arguing that leasehold's problem is unenforced rights.
